cells.tense: Right now the change you want is already in motion, and the patience is yours to keep.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Put on paper what a shared practice is meant to carry and what it does now, then follow that page for a week.
cells.core:
You are in the middle of a change in shared meaning, and it is going one small piece at a time. That is what makes it hold; a tradition does not turn by announcement. The work gets fed by your own steady attention rather than your worry about it, and a thing being handled instead of forced can be felt from outside.

Put the inquiry on paper where others can see the shape of it. Ask what the practice is meant to carry and what it does now, and set the answers down in plain words. If you cannot tell yet, leave the gap visible. Someone else will read the page differently, and you will find out which parts were yours alone. That is what keeps a shared thing breathing instead of closing. The clarity you keep asking the tradition for is already something you can make, and it goes down in plain words.
cells.sheetLine: The change is already moving, one small piece at a time.
cells.verb: forcing structural change into shared meaning, slow but unstoppable
cells.place: in the shared meaning and tradition you belong to

cells.tense: Tomorrow's version of the shared thing has already arrived in your head, and you are bracing against it.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Before the next gathering, pick what the ritual is for, then carry that with one other person even if it comes out rough.
cells.core:
You can see a shape for the shared thing so clearly that the present version feels like a failure. You keep pushing, and the pressure on the tradition grows with it. The structure you want is real. It is also still being built, and the force you are using arrives with you.

Do the thing in front of someone before you have it right. Pick one part that matters and carry it through with another person, badly if that is what today allows. The doing is the teaching, and the teaching is how the meaning gets passed; it cannot be passed on a plan alone. Let the hands do the rest. That is the way back: breakthrough that comes from something real instead of from the force you are applying.

cells.tense: You are still at a door of shared meaning that is already behind you.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Find a wrongness in how a shared practice runs and correct it yourself, with no announcement and no one's permission.
cells.core:
Where you take part in shared meaning, the energy for it has drained out. You still show up, but the part that threw weight behind a change is absent, and so the tradition gets agreement from you instead of force. The structures you could see falling are unmoved, not because they should be, but because the push isn't coming.

Make the correction. Not the big reform, the wrongness you have been walking around. Fix it yourself, tell no one, and that is the whole of it. A decisive act done in the open does not require approval. The charge that comes back is the point. One move makes the next move possible, and the direction you did not feel last week is on the other side of doing it.
cells.sheetLine: You still show up, but the force is gone.
cells.verb: forcing structural change into shared meaning, slow but unstoppable
cells.place: in the shared meaning and tradition you belong to

cells.tense: The pen is down in a shared room you are already writing in.
cells.act: tend the fire without burning out
cells.ask: Keep a shared practice you care about alive without asking it for anything; if it burns, rest and return rather than abandon it.
cells.core:
You are already changing the shared thing. The initiative is in your hands, and your own account of it leaves that out, so it looks like duty instead of steering. You do not see the effect you are having on the people who carry the same meaning, and you keep waiting for a sign that it is legitimate to want this.

Keep one part of it warm with steady care. Direction comes from real engagement rather than from the permission you keep looking for. If it burns, stop and come back instead of quitting the thing. No announcement is needed. In time the work shows what it is, and the thing you are already keeping can be yours.
cells.sheetLine: You are already changing it. Your own account just leaves that out.
